reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) comes entirely from a first-principles study on NiCoCr medium-entropy alloys, which have an FCC structure, not the BCC refractory MoNbTaW system. The claims about octahedral site preference, stress field modification, and dislocation glide effects are specific to NiCoCr and are not supported by any prior evidence on refractory HEAs. The hypothesis extrapolates these findings to a fundamentally different crystal structure and alloy system without direct evidence, and the cited passages do not address carbide suppression or the proposed mechanism in BCC alloys.
premises: Carbon occupies octahedral interstitial sites in the BCC MoNbTaW lattice
Interstitial carbon reduces heterogeneous stress fields and locally lowers barriers for edge dislocation glide
This promotes uniform dislocation motion, reducing strain localization and enhancing ductility
The effect is similar to that observed in other alloy systems (e.g., NiCoCr)
An optimized heat treatment can keep carbon in solution and suppress carbide precipitation
